<description>
**Problem:** Processes connected to `bitcoin-node` over IPC (with `-ipcbind`) can use the `Mining` interface, but they can't currently use the `Chain` interface to read chain data or follow chain events. Chain data could be useful to third-party clients and Bitcoin Core's own wallet could use this as well to run in a separate process (#10102). But exposing all of `interfaces::Chain` to external clients would make its methods hard to change, since the wallet uses them as internal API (#34981).

**Solution:** Add capnp wrappers for `interfaces::Chain`, split into two interfaces backed by the same C++ class:

- `Chain`, returned by `Init.makeChain`, is stable. It follows Cap'n Proto schema evolution rules, so existing clients keep working as methods are added. It starts with the five block lookup methods: `findBlock`, `findFirstBlockWithTimeAndHeight`, `findAncestorByHeight`, `findAncestorByHash` and `findCommonAncestor`.
- `UnstableChain`, returned by `Init.makeUnstableChain`, extends `Chain` with every other method, for Bitcoin Core's internal C++ callers, such as the wallet, communicating over IPC. It can change in any way between releases. Incompatible changes renumber `makeUnstableChain`, so old clients get an error instead of calling the wrong methods.

Methods can move from `UnstableChain` to `Chain` once we're willing to support them for external use. `test/functional/interface_ipc.py` shows a Python client calling both interfaces. Like the existing IPC interfaces, these are only available to processes that can connect to the IPC socket, which already grants full node access through `Init.makeRpc`.

**Merge order:** This depends on bitcoin-core/libmultiprocess#377 and a subtree update that includes it (this PR currently carries that subtree change as its first commit), and on #36520, which fixes node crashes IPC clients could trigger with invalid `Chain` arguments.

---

This PR is part of the [process separation project](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/issues/28722).

**This is based on a `src/ipc/libmultiprocess` subtree update to d1aff664fa2.** The non-base commits are:

- [`d7b18a34727` ipc: Add capnp serialization code for bitcoin types](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/29409/commits/d7b18a34727144e14735a003b7f3573497b26c52)
- [`5dfb5b32dec` ipc: Add capnp wrapper for Handler interface](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/29409/commits/5dfb5b32decdadcb02a8a7f02fbbbf9e199e752c)
- [`105b9f54877` interfaces, refactor: Change Chain method signatures for IPC wrappers](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/29409/commits/105b9f54877c92e8d3d20b4e25058cb30f7c0ca8)
- [`2f17601940b` interfaces: Fix findFirstBlockWithTimeAndHeight and FoundBlock::locator comments](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/29409/commits/2f17601940bded96a485a7620fbd136e8a822ef6)
- [`06588f78312` ipc: Add capnp wrappers for stable Chain and UnstableChain interfaces](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/29409/commits/06588f78312dd2ab2ff87f62c6f55cf2aa37affd)

105b9f5487 interfaces, refactor: Change Chain method signatures for IPC wrappers

Drop const from Chain::getFeeRateEstimate() and
Chain::maximumFeeEstimationTargetBlocks(), and pass the
Chain::updateRwSetting() update function by value, so libmultiprocess can
generate an IPC client class implementing them. Generated client methods are
never const, so they can't override const virtual methods, and the generated
server code can only pass a callback argument to the implementation by value.

2f17601940 interfaces: Fix findFirstBlockWithTimeAndHeight and FoundBlock::locator comments

Make the comments match what the code does, now that these methods are part
of the stable Chain IPC interface and external clients rely on them:

- findFirstBlockWithTimeAndHeight compares the given time with
  CBlockIndex::GetBlockTimeMax(), the highest timestamp of the block and its
  ancestors, not with the block's own timestamp. Since block timestamps can
  go backwards, it can return a block whose own timestamp is lower than the
  given time.

- FoundBlock::locator returns a locator for any block, including one that is
  not in the active chain. The comment matched the documentation of
  CChain::GetLocator() when it was written ("Return a CBlockLocator that
  refers to a block in this chain"), although that function already returned
  correct locators for blocks outside the chain, following their own branch
  with CBlockIndex::GetAncestor(). Commit
  ed470940cddbeb40425960d51cefeec4948febe4 from bitcoin/bitcoin#25717
  replaced it with a GetLocator() function documented for any block index
  entry, and this comment was not updated.

Suggested by enirox001 in
https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/29409#discussion_r4479592320 and
https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/29409#discussion_r4479715634

This change was written with Claude Opus 5.5.

06588f7831 ipc: Add capnp wrappers for stable Chain and UnstableChain interfaces

Add a stable Chain capnp interface for external clients, and an UnstableChain
interface extending it for Bitcoin Core's internal C++ callers, such as the
wallet, communicating over IPC. Both are backed by the C++ interfaces::Chain
class. Stable Chain methods follow Cap'n Proto schema evolution rules so
existing clients keep working as methods are added. UnstableChain methods can
change in any way between releases, as discussed in bitcoin/bitcoin#34981.

The stable interface starts out with only the block lookup methods that use
FoundBlockParam/FoundBlockResult (findBlock, findFirstBlockWithTimeAndHeight,
findAncestorByHeight, findAncestorByHash, findCommonAncestor). Other methods
can be moved to it from UnstableChain when they are ready for external use.

This change was written with Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context).

0d81792278 ipc: Expose Chain interface

Add Init.makeChain and Init.makeUnstableChain methods returning the stable
Chain and UnstableChain interfaces to external processes spawning or
connecting to bitcoin-node, and test them in interface_ipc.py.

This change was written with Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context).
